'''Yitzhak Apeloig''' ({{Langx|he|יצחק אפלויג}}; 1 September 1944 – 28 May 2026) was an Israeli scholar who was a pioneer in the [[computational chemistry]] field of the [[Ab initio quantum chemistry methods]] for predicting and preparing the physical and chemical properties of materials.<ref>{{cite web|title=Technion President Yitzhak Apeloig to Receive Chemical Society Prize – American Society for Technion-Israel Institute of Technology|url=http://www.ats.org/site/News2?page=NewsArticle&id=6099&security=1&news_iv_ctrl=1461|access-date=27 November 2013|archive-date=3 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203010036/http://www.ats.org/site/News2?page=NewsArticle&id=6099&security=1&news_iv_ctrl=1461|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was the president of the [[Technion]] from 2001 until 2009 where the position was handed off to [[Peretz Lavie]]. Apeloig held the Joseph Israel Freund Chair in Chemistry and was the co-director of the Lise Meitner Minerva Center for Computational Quantum Chemistry at the Technion. He served as dean of the Faculty of Chemistry from 1995 to 1999, where he was named Teacher of the Year at three occasions.

During his Technion presidency, Apeloig recruited more than 150 elite scholars and scientists worldwide to the Technion.<ref name=ATS>{{cite web|title=Nobel Laureate Delivers First Apeloig Lectureship – American Society for Technion-Israel Institute of Technology|url=http://www.ats.org/site/News2?page=NewsArticle&id=7746|access-date=27 November 2013|archive-date=3 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203014424/http://www.ats.org/site/News2?page=NewsArticle&id=7746|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also established a number of interdisciplinary research centers such as the [[Russell Berrie Nanotechnology Institute]]. He also established the Lorry I. Lokey Interdisciplinary Center for Life Sciences and Engineering. In 2010 was inducted to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=ATS /> The same year he also became a recipient of the [[Frederic Stanley Kipping]] Award in Silicon Chemistry.<ref>{{cite web|title=Frederic Stanley Kipping Award in Silicon Chemistry|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/frederic-stanley-kipping-award-in-silicon-chemistry.html|publisher=ACS|access-date=27 November 2013}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Apeloig was born in [[Bukhara]], [[Uzbek SSR]] on 1 September 1944,<ref name=tech2>{{cite web|title=Apeloig Yitzhak Web Site – Technion|url=http://www.admin.technion.ac.il/ApeloigYitzhak/|access-date=27 November 2013|archive-date=15 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180215113549/http://www.admin.technion.ac.il/ApeloigYitzhak/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="acs.org">{{cite web |title=Yitzhak Apeloig bio |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/85/i25/Yitzhak-Apeloig.html |website=cen.acs.org |date=21 January 2025 }}</ref> after his family fled from the [[Nazis]] following the [[invasion of Poland]] in September 1939. In 1947, when he was three years old, the family immigrated to Israel.<ref name="acs.org" /> He served in the [[Nahal Brigade]] and the [[paratroopers]] between 1962 and 1964. He studied chemistry and physics at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], and completed his undergraduate (receiving his BA in physics and chemistry in 1967, and his masters in 1969) and graduate education there, including a Ph.D. in chemistry in 1974.<ref name="acs.org" /> He conducted postdoctoral research at [[Princeton University]] with [[Paul v. R. Schleyer]] and collaborated with Nobel Laureate [[John A. Pople]].<ref name="acs.org" /> Apeloig joined the faculty of the Technion in 1976 and in 1983 he was appointed a professor. He became the dean of the Faculty of Chemistry in 1995 until 2001 when he became the president of the Technion, replacing [[Amos Lapidot]].<ref name="technionil">{{cite web |url=https://www.technion.ac.il/en/former-presidents/ |title=President &#124; Technion – Israel Institute of Technology |work=Technion - Israel Institute of Technology |date=9 August 2015 |access-date=16 February 2020 |archive-date=4 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704050200/https://www.technion.ac.il/en/former-presidents/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2009 he was followed as president by [[Peretz Lavie]].<ref name="technionil"/>

Yitzhak Apeloig died in [[Haifa]] in 28 May 2026, at the age of 81.<ref>{{Cite web |last=קירשטיין |first=רולי |date=2026-05-28 |title=נשיא הטכניון לשעבר הלך לעולמו |url=https://www.colbonews.co.il/academy/209975/ |access-date=2026-05-29 |website=כלבו – חיפה והקריות |language=he}}</ref>
